verses.text: Then Bildad from Shuah answered:
"How long will you keep searching for words? Think first, and then we can talk.
Why do you treat us like animals? Why do you think we are stupid?
You tear yourself apart in your anger. Should the earth be left empty just for you? Should the rocks be moved from their places for you?
The light of the wicked will be put out. The flame of his fire will stop burning.
The light in his tent will become dark. The lamp beside him will go out.
His strong steps will become weak. His own plans will trip him up.
His own feet lead him into a net, and he walks right into its holes.
A trap grabs him by the heel. A snare holds him tight.
A rope is hidden on the ground for him, and a trap lies on his path.
Terrors frighten him on every side and chase him at every step.
He is weak from hunger, and disaster is ready for him when he falls.
Disease eats away his skin. Death's firstborn eats away his arms and legs.
He is torn from the safety of his tent and marched off to the king of terrors.
Strangers live in his tent, and burning sulfur is scattered over his home.
His roots dry up below, and his branches wither above.
No one on earth remembers him. No one in the land knows his name.
He is driven from light into darkness and chased out of the world.
He has no children or grandchildren among his people, and no one is left where he once lived.
People who come after him are shocked at what happened to him, just as those who lived before were terrified.
This is surely what happens to the homes of evil people. This is the fate of those who do not know God."
